data.hypothesis: The first-pass four-accumulator variant measured 5.26604e-7 seconds versus 5.25586e-7 for the single-accumulator two-pass version, a small difference that does not establish an effect. This experiment keeps the single vector-minimum recurrence and instead unrolls the equality search across four vectors before checking for a match. Reducing loop and mask-check frequency may help when the search prefix is long, but loading a whole group can waste work on earlier matches; random and decreasing inputs may therefore behave differently.

memory_lessons.applicability: The next contrast should target a different pass than the already-tested first-pass accumulator unrolling.
memory_lessons.claim: Both two-pass variants were correct. The four-accumulator variant measured 5.26604e-7 seconds versus 5.25586e-7 for the single-accumulator variant; this small difference alone does not establish whether accumulator unrolling helps.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Validate the four-vector equality-search unroll, then compare repeated timings with attention to random and decreasing inputs.

data.notes: This changes only src/candidate.cpp and preserves the supplied interface and signed minimum/tie behavior, including scalar tails and the n <= 0 behavior of the original scan. The target facts specify AMD EPYC 9654 and GCC 14.2; an earlier T2 AVX-512 candidate was valid on the frozen protocol. I did not compile or run this candidate, so the controller must check build and correctness before comparing repeated timings, especially across random and decreasing cases.
transformations: Compute the signed int32 minimum with one AVX-512 minimum accumulator and reduce it, including a scalar tail.
Search from index zero using four unrolled AVX-512 equality comparisons per group; choose the earliest matching vector and lowest matching lane.
Retain a vector remainder scan and scalar tail so incomplete groups and all valid lengths are handled.
